proposals.claim: Plain linen fabrics can be reliably classified by surface texture analysis from catalogue photography without requiring physical samples
proposals.rationale: Catalogue photography with standardized lighting conditions captures surface characteristics distinctive to plain linens (slub frequency, yarn irregularity, light reflection patterns) that correlate with quality grades and fibre source origins
constraints: Photography must use consistent backlighting and sidelighting angles
Minimum 4x optical zoom resolution required to resolve individual yarns
Images must be taken within 24 hours of production batch creation
Classification must remain conditional pending physical hand-feel verification
evidenceNeeded: Standardized photography protocol documentation showing lighting setup, camera settings, and zoom specifications
Cross-reference samples of classified fabrics with independently verified supplier certifications
Digital comparison matrix showing visual signatures of different linen qualities from known origins
Photographic baseline standards for each classification grade tested against 50+ catalogue images

proposals.claim: Print pattern scale and repeat measurement from catalogue photography can establish fibre source provenance when combined with supplier documentation
proposals.rationale: Pattern repeat dimensions, screen registration precision, and color separation quality visible in high-resolution catalogue imagery correlate with specific production facilities and technical capabilities that have documented geographical origins
constraints: Pattern analysis limited to printed fabrics with geometric or measurable repeats only
Provenance claims require cross-validation with supplier mill certifications and dye-lot records
Photography angle must be perpendicular to fabric surface with calibrated scale reference
Analysis cannot determine fibre type or country of origin independently
evidenceNeeded: High-resolution catalogue photography with embedded scale reference (minimum 600 DPI)
Supplier documentation linking pattern repeats to specific printing facilities
Documented printing capability specifications for 10+ known production locations
Verification samples from claimed origin mills with matching pattern signatures

proposals.claim: Unknown fibre content in blended linens can be classified into probability categories using visual and photographic characteristics without making absolute fibre composition claims
proposals.rationale: Luster patterns, yarn twist consistency, and surface pilling behavior visible in catalogue photography provide indicators for fibre category hypotheses (linen-rich vs. cotton-rich vs. synthetic-blend) requiring laboratory confirmation
constraints: Classification must be explicitly labeled as 'probability-based pending lab testing'
Cannot claim specific percentage compositions without supplier testing certificates
Visual analysis cannot distinguish between fibre types with identical lustre properties
Photography artifacts (gloss, shadow, angle) can create false indicators and must be documented
evidenceNeeded: Controlled photographic comparison series showing luster signatures of known fibre blends (50/50, 60/40, 75/25 ratios)
Lab test results (FTIR or fibre microscopy) from 30+ sample fabrics with corresponding catalogue images
Documentation of visual misclassifications that have occurred with similar visual profiles
Supplier witness testing protocol for unknown fibre validation

proposals.claim: Catalogue photography can establish plausible GSM weight ranges for unknown linen fabrics by comparing yarn density and colour saturation indicators
proposals.rationale: Yarn count visibility, fabric hand opacity shown through backlighting, and dye saturation patterns correlate with typical weight ranges in commercial linen production (100-400 GSM for fashion linens), establishing investigation boundaries rather than precise measurements
constraints: GSM estimation limited to ±50 point uncertainty range minimum
Cannot claim exact weight values from photography alone
Estimates valid only for plain-weave linens; complex weaves require structural analysis
Saturation-based estimates unreliable for overdyed or reactive-dyed fabrics
evidenceNeeded: Photographic comparison library of 20+ linen fabrics with certified GSM values and corresponding imagery
Documented correlation analysis between yarn visibility/density in photos and actual measured weights
Supplier specification sheets showing typical GSM ranges for visual categories
Technical note on saturation levels and their limits in weight estimation accuracy

proposals.claim: Formal 60/75 Lea shirting and suiting linens can be validated for count specification through documented supplier certification and pattern consistency without requiring physical thread count analysis
proposals.rationale: 60-75 Lea specifications (approximately 80-100 thread count per inch) are manufacturing standards documented by suppliers; catalogue photography showing pattern regularity combined with supplier attestation provides evidence for specification conformance when physical testing unavailable
constraints: Specification claim requires primary supplier documentation as mandatory supporting evidence
Catalogue photography can show regularity consistency but cannot measure actual Lea count independently
Formal grade claims require thread count verification certificates from original supplier
Visual uniformity alone insufficient; supplier historical production records required
evidenceNeeded: Original supplier specification sheets for the specific fabric line photographed
Thread count test certificates (within 12 months of catalogue image date) from accredited testing laboratory
Catalogue image date alignment with supplier batch production documentation
Written supplier attestation linking specific SKU to 60 or 75 Lea classification

proposals.claim: Linen-blend composition percentages stated in catalogues must be verified against supplier test certificates and batch records before acceptance as factual claims
proposals.rationale: Visual appearance of linen-blend fabrics varies significantly based on actual fibre percentages; catalogue descriptions can contain aspirational or outdated information requiring independent supplier documentation to establish accuracy
constraints: No blend percentage claims accepted without corresponding laboratory test evidence
Supplier attestation alone insufficient without supporting lab data from accredited facilities
Batch numbers and test dates must align with catalogue publication dates within 6-month window
Changes in supplier formulations invalidate historical catalogue specifications
evidenceNeeded: Laboratory test certificates (FTIR or wet chemical analysis) for each claimed blend ratio
Supplier batch records showing fibre sourcing dates and percentage formulations
Documented cases where catalogue claims differed from test-verified compositions
Verification protocol for establishing which supplier certifications are current and valid

proposals.claim: Catalogue fabric images must be verified as representing current active stock items with available inventory before proposing them for sourcing or specification decisions
proposals.rationale: Catalogue photographs often remain published long after stock depletion, production discontinuation, or supplier changeovers; visual authenticity requires matching current inventory records with image publication dates to confirm actual availability
constraints: Catalogue age limit: images older than 12 months require current stock confirmation from supplier
Visual similarity between photographs does not confirm product identity or availability
Stock status changes rapidly in fashion; weekly verification required for sourcing decisions
Archived/historical fabric images must be clearly labeled as such in all proposals
evidenceNeeded: Current supplier inventory management system documentation showing stock status for catalogued SKUs
Correlation between catalogue image publication dates and supplier production/stock records
Documented cases of catalogue images remaining available for discontinued products
Supplier communication protocol for confirming active status of specific fabric lines

proposals.claim: All linen fabric classification proposals based on catalogue photography must explicitly disclose photography conditions, processing, and known limitations as evidence context
proposals.rationale: Catalogue photographs undergo color correction, contrast enhancement, and digital processing that can misrepresent actual fabric properties; transparent disclosure of these conditions is essential for evaluating reliability of visual evidence-based claims
constraints: Photography condition documentation mandatory for every catalogue-based proposal
Post-processing treatments (brightness, saturation, sharpening) must be specified or acknowledged as unknown
Lighting type (studio, window, flash) and angle must be documented when known
Unknown photography conditions require explicit notation and reduce evidence reliability rating
evidenceNeeded: Catalogue image metadata analysis report identifying color profile, compression, and known processing
Photographer/production documentation describing intended color representation protocols
Side-by-side comparison of same fabric in raw catalogue photo vs. actual physical sample
Guidelines establishing reliability tiers based on photography documentation completeness
